key_insight: Co2In improves continual learning by separating fast adaptive learning in working memory from durable retention in long-term memory, then consolidating and integrating learned knowledge into compact representations.
engineering_relevance: For data-driven constitutive modeling, this suggests a practical route to update material models with new experiments while reducing catastrophic forgetting of previously learned behaviors.
method: Working memory learns new-task parameters from incoming data to preserve plasticity.
Consolidation extracts patterns from learned parameters into compact knowledge representations.
Integrated long-term memory stores transformed knowledge in separate network layers for stable retention.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet in exemplar-free Class-IL and Task-IL settings, where it achieved state-of-the-art performance with efficient memory use.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of consolidation and integration; in real deployments, added architectural complexity may increase implementation and tuning burden.
paper_title: Co2In: a Bi-level Memory Incremental Learning Framework with Knowledge Encoding, Consolidation, and Integration
